pr_body:
Right now if you boot up MeiliSearch and point it to a DB directory created with a previous version of MeiliSearch the existing indexes will be deleted. This [used to be](https://github.com/meilisearch/MeiliSearch/commit/51d7c84e7327b14f84522a1f5521f6d98c398a6f) prevented by a startup check which would compare the current engine version vs what was stored in the DB directory's version file, but this functionality seems to have been lost after a few refactorings of the code.

In order to go back to the old behavior we'll need to reintroduce the `VERSION` file that used to be present; I considered reusing the `metadata.json` file used in the dumps feature, but this seemed like the simpler and more approach. As the intent is just to restore functionality, the implementation is quite basic. I imagine that in the future we could build on this and do things like compatibility across major/minor versions and even migrating between formats.

Closes #1840

issue_context.title: MeiliSearch removes indexes when `data.ms` is not compatible
issue_context.body:
Steps to reproduce
- Start MeiliSearch v0.22.0
- Add documents
- Stop MeiliSearch v0.22.0 and run MeiliSearch v0.23.0 using the same `data.ms`

-> MeiliSearch starts without any error, but should not, and remove the indexes in `data.ms`

MeiliSearch should display the following error
```
Cannot open database, expected MeiliSearch engine version: X.X.X, current engine version Y.Y.Y
```
at it was before, and should not start if data.ms is not compatible without removing the indexes
comments:
If this is still valid, I'd like to take it!

EDIT: So taking a look into the issue, it seems like we need a way of seeing if the `data.ms` is from a previous version or not. With MeiliSearch's dump functionality I see that there is a metadata.json that gets spit out as part of that process, but I am not sure if there is a similar process for `data.ms`.

If not, I _think_ I would need to add that as a first step before being able to do the desired check-and-fail behavior. Unless perhaps there is another way?

If I'm not mistaken there used to be a file in the db folder that contained the version, that we used to check against the current version. It might still be there, and in any case this is a regression

Wanted to share this experience (which might be related):

### Our environment
* Running Meilisearch on Ubuntu 20.04 with Docker using the "latest" image tag (`getmeili/meilisearch`)
* Our `data.ms` database is mounted via Docker Volumes

### What happened
* We originally built indexes on `v0.23.1`
* Everything worked great
* Our Meilisearch instance automatically updated to `v0.24.0`
* All of our indexes disappeared

### How we were able to get our indexes back
* We forced our image to go back to **v0.23.1**

I am also going to cc @danpastori on this issue since I am the sysadmin and he is the developer who helped me troubleshoot this 😁

Any additional information on this, please let me know!
